text:
maria: Heads-up — hotfix canary (v3) started in eu-west and I'm seeing a spike in 500s, p50 still ok but p95 & error-rate are nudging thresholds. I'm going to close the traffic gate and do a fast handoff to v2.

deploy-bot: Canary started: model=v3, traffic=3%, region=eu-west, id=cb-1902223344

aj: ack. good call. for the rollback we should do: 1) close gate -> stop new canary traffic 2) shift traffic to fallback pool (v2-dedupe) with prewarm 3) drain KV/session cache from canary nodes -> reuse prefixes on fallback nodes 4) monitor errors and cost.

maria: plan: 1) gate=true 2) traffic-shift API to fallback with prewarm 3) async cache-handoff 4) short TTL on session tokens so state collapses quickly. running now.

sasha: question on the API: should the console "Rollback" button call /admin/traffic-shift? currently there's an enum: {mode: "graceful" | "immediate"}. we debated force=true earlier. i prefer explicit modes so UI can show "drain + handoff" vs "cut traffic".

aj: +1 on explicit modes. also add telemetry checkpoint events so the rollout timeline shows: gate_closed, traffic_shift_started, cache_handoff_started, cache_evicted, traffic_shift_complete. we need those to surface on the rollout trace.

anya: prewarm note — before shifting all remaining canary traffic, warm 1 GPU in fallback with the same model/quantization to avoid p99 spike. put a 30s warmup window.

maria: executing traffic-shift now. payload: ```\nPOST /internal/v1/admin/traffic-shift\n{\n  \"from\": \"v3-eu-west-canary\",\n  \"to\": \"v2-eu-west-fallback\",\n  \"percent\": 100,\n  \"mode\": \"graceful\",\n  \"prewarm\": true\n}\n```\n\ndeploy-bot: Traffic shift request accepted (op=op-1902223344). prewarm triggered.

sasha: small API debate: should the endpoint return a job id only or also schedule a safety-auto-revert? i worry operators will forget to watch. automatic revert on X errors in 5m seems useful.

aj: can we default to safety-auto-revert with an opt-out flag? most teams want protection, but make it transparent in the console and on the job.

maria: enabling safety-auto-revert = true for this run. thresholds: error_rate > 2% (5m window) OR p95 latency > 1200ms.

deploy-bot: prewarm complete. cache-handoff starting. cache-handoff command: ```\nPOST /internal/cache/handoff\n{\n  \"source\": \"v3-eu-west-canary\",\n  \"target\": \"v2-eu-west-fallback\",\n  \"strategy\": \"prefix-move\",\n  \"evict_after\": \"60s\"\n}\n```\n\naj: note: prefix-move will keep most KV entries; evict_after ensures we don't keep stale ephemeral sessions. watch mem usage on fallback.

maria: cache-handoff reported 92% successful prefix transfers, 8% misses. starting traffic cutover.

deploy-bot: traffic_shift_complete (op=op-1902223344). new default traffic routing -> v2-eu-west-fallback.

anya: looks stable on dashboards: error-rate down to baseline, p95 back under 700ms. nice. :tada:

sasha: follow-up for UX: add a small modal when you click Rollback explaining what happens to caches and sessions and offering options: \n- \"Immediate cut\" (force)\n- \"Graceful handoff\" (default)\n- \"Graceful + safety-auto-revert\"\n
aj: also show estimated token-cost delta during rollback and whether dedupe cache will be reused. helps product decisions.

maria: thanks all. final note — session tokens created during canary will be short-lived. we'll run a background sweep for orphan sessions in 30m. closing thread.

sasha: adding an internal RFC issue to eng-platform to standardize api param names and rollout telemetry contract.

maria: great, thanks :heart:
